title: Leaderboards
description: Allow comparison between public models through transparent, category-based rankings with filtering, historical tracking and full score transparency.
rationale: Leaderboards create engagement and a feedback loop: users iterate to climb rankings, surfacing high-quality public models and demonstrating the trade-offs between competing policy goals.
success_criteria: Each category lists public models ranked by the relevant deterministic score
Filtering narrows results without changing ranking semantics
Each ranked entry exposes the score and rationale behind its position
Historical ranking snapshots are retained and viewable
notes:
## Scope (in)
- Categories: Best Social Fairness, Best Economic Growth, Best Fiscal Sustainability, Best NHS Outcome, Best Housing Outcome, Best Balanced Model
- Ranking logic
- Filtering
- Historical tracking
- Score transparency

## Out of scope
- Determining scores (EPIC-003)
- Making models public (EPIC-006)
- Monte Carlo / benchmarking research views (EPIC-014)

## Dependencies
- EPIC-003 - rankings sort by deterministic category scores
- EPIC-006 - only public models are eligible to rank

## Assumptions
- Only public models appear; unlisted/private excluded
- Rankings derived purely from deterministic scores (no AI)
- 'Best Balanced' uses a documented composite of categories

## Risks
- Gaming the rankings -> transparent criteria; deterministic scores; optional review
- Ranking feels opaque -> always show score + rationale behind a rank
- Performance at scale -> precompute/cache rankings; index by category
- Historical data growth -> defined retention/aggregation strategy

## Future extensions
- Seasonal / time-boxed competitions
- Per-region or per-theme leaderboards
- Benchmarking against reference models (links to EPIC-014)
